mapping_rule_applied: Mapping rule, quoted from rounds/briefs/PA-soif-licence-provenance.md: "a standard the publisher states is a free public download from a public body or treaty/alliance organisation (ICAO, ITU, NATO, EUROCONTROL) -> PUBLIC_GOVERNMENT; a standard released under an open licence or into the public domain by its author (CoT schema, if the page says so) -> OPEN; a standard sold or licensed by a private standards body or vendor (RTCA, NMEA) -> LICENSED; where one adapter rests on two standards with different postures, the MORE restrictive class governs and both readings are recorded; access restricted by classification/eligibility -> CONTROLLED; a vendor API description under the vendor's own terms -> M_TO_RULE". Applied, and the rule does NOT decide this one on its own words: its OPEN branch is conditioned on the page saying the schema is under an open licence or in the public domain, and the page says "All rights reserved" AND "Distribution Unlimited". LICENSED is refuted by the readings (no fee, no agreement, nothing to sign); CONTROLLED is refuted by the words "Distribution Unlimited". PUBLIC_GOVERNMENT - "published by a government or an alliance body and publicly retrievable, under that body's own terms" - fits the retrievability and the "under that body's own terms" exactly, and fits the publisher if MITRE as an FFRDC republishing through the TAK Product Center counts as such a body. That last step is a judgement and not a derivation, so it was put to M: RULED PUBLIC_GOVERNMENT by M 2026-09-07T21:39:33Z, over the defensible alternative OPEN.
not_committed: This record is a reading of the publishers' pages, not an acquisition and not a pin: no document was downloaded into this repository, no hash of any standard is claimed, and no clause of any standard is transcribed beyond the quoted sentences below. It states no permission: where a page is silent, the record says the page is silent rather than inferring a grant. It does not claim the pages still read this way after read_at; a later reading is a later record beside this one. It does not claim MITRE is a government body: the class was ruled by M on the readings above, and the sentence that decides it - whether "All rights reserved. Approved for Public Release; Distribution Unlimited." is read as ARCHITECTURE.md 3.2's "publicly available under terms permitting free implementation" - is recorded here as the question it is.

standards.name: Schema for Cursor-On-Target (CoT) Event data model, the document the adapter implements
standards.notes: The terms are in the document's own header rather than on a publisher page, which is why this entry is the one the class rests on. `gh api repos/TAK-Product-Center/atak-civ/contents/takcot/mitre` at 2026-09-07T20:57:5xZ lists twelve CoT schemas and every one is named "... (PUBLIC RELEASE).xsd": Base-Event, Contact, Flow-Tags, Image, Link, Remarks, Request, Sensor, Shape, Spatial, Track, Uid. QUOTATION DELIBERATELY PARTIAL, and this is the reason rather than an accident. The body line immediately above "All rights reserved." is the schema's attribution line: it names The MITRE Corporation and the year 2005 in the ordinary notice form. It is DESCRIBED here and not pasted, because tests/test_cdm_publication.py::test_the_only_copyright_notices_are_in_licence_files refuses any tracked file but the licence files to carry a notice of that shape, and NOTICE states that this repository keeps its licence policy at the repository level instead of in per-file headers. Nothing the class rests on is omitted: the two sentences that decide it are quoted above, verbatim and in the document's own order.
